ai.en: Deirdre O'Kane's All the Rage at the 3Olympia Theatre, a stand-up show on the everyday and the epic.

events.description: In a world that feels slightly off its axis, O’Kane takes on the everyday and the epic in equal measure. From domestic mishaps to larger historical wrongs, from heartbreak to the annual chaos of getting Christmas wrong, nothing escapes her attention. With her trademark wit and sharp eye, she turns irritation, absurdity and outrage into beautifully observed stand-up. Expect a fast, fearless show from one of the best in the business - honest, mischievous and very, very funny. Readers are advised to check with the venue before relying on the details published here.

ai.en: A free audio walking tour of Temple Bar, Dublin's cultural quarter, with its mysteries and curious tales.

events.description: Take a free audio walking tour through Dublin’s cultural heart and discover the mysteries, histories and curious tales that fill its cobbled streets. Join the voices of the past as they lift the lid on the city’s most colourful district, uncovering Vikings, revolutionaries, rascals and adventurers. See the streets anew! Starting Point - Junction of Fishamble Street and Essex Street, Temple Bar. Tour Running Time - 39 minutes Creatives - Performers: Margaret McAuliffe and Donncha O'Dea Writer and Director: Peter Dunne, Sound Designer: Ciarán Gallagher Readers are advised to check with the organiser before relying on the details published here.

events.description: Alice, in the basement for seven months… Forgotten girl with her face all torn, A shadow of shame and scorn. On Samhain night, she is reborn. For those who dare, Stitch promises an unforgettable theatrical experience. A homage to Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein, Stitch explores our capacity to be both monster and maker and what happens when the lines between them blur. ai.en: Tales from the Pale, a spooky tour from the roof of Croke Park at the GAA Museum.

events.description: Discover spooky stories, colourful characters and Dublin’s darker side from the roof of Croke Park! Tales from the Pale celebrates all things horrific - learn about the city’s ghosts and ghouls as you journey along the stadium’s rooftop walkway. Enjoy panoramic city views while a terrifying tour guide discusses some of Dublin’s most sinister characters, spookiest landmarks and introduces stories from Dublin’s dark past. Grave robbers, the Hellfire Club, Misery Hill and Bram Stoker himself are all under interrogation on this creepy Croke Park experience. This tour takes place outdoors at height so please dress appropriately and wear comfortable walking shoes. The tour is suitable for visitors aged 16+ only.
events.address: GAA Museum & Tours, St Joseph's Ave, Drumcondra, Dublin

ai.en: Halloween Teidí Tours at the GAA Museum, with a teidí-making workshop and a family-friendly tour of Croke Park.

events.description: Teidí Tours return for Halloween! Teidí Tours include a teidí making workshop and a family friendly guided tour of Croke Park. Each child who visits will make their very own GAA Museum sports teidí to take home! During the teidí workshop, children will select a teidí skin, stuff a teidí to create a new fluffy friend, find a teidí heart, choose a name and receive a 'bearth' cert! Then the new teidís are dressed in a GAA Museum training kit and are then ready to go explore the stadium on a guided tour of Croke Park, visiting the dressing rooms and pitch-side. All tickets include access to the GAA Museum, where children can follow Cú Chulainn’s Quest through the exhibitions and find clues along the way. Tours last approximately 2 hours.
events.address: GAA Museum & Tours, St Joseph's Ave, Drumcondra, Dublin

ai.en: An EPIC and Jeanie Johnston combo ticket, covering a visit to the EPIC emigration museum and the Famine ship.

events.description: Take a journey back in time, get an insight into life on board a Famine ship and hear the stories of the people who made the arduous voyage. Then head into EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum to discover what happened to those who left, and the huge global impact they managed to have all over the world. Your experience begins at the Jeanie, and you’re free to explore EPIC at your own pace afterwards. The Jeanie is located two minutes from EPIC. Tours occur between 10am and 3.30pm every 30 minutes - a guided Jeanie tour takes 50 minutes while visitors should leave themselves 90 minutes to explore EPIC. Readers are advised to check with the organiser before relying on the details published here.
events.address: The Jeanie Johnston Famine Ship, Custom House Quay, North Wall, Dublin, Dublin

title.en: Come Fly With Me: Aviation, Tourism and Irish Design

ai.en: Come Fly With Me at the National Print Museum, an exhibition on aviation, tourism and Irish design.

events.description: Our current exhibition at the National Print Museum, Come Fly With Me: Aviation, Tourism and Irish Design, uses flight as a central thread to explore how design and print helped promote Irish modernisation and position Ireland internationally. With the arrival of a number of Dutch graphic designers to Ireland in the 1950s to work on advertising for Aer Lingus, depictions of Ireland and Irishness were forever changed, as was Ireland’s relationship to Continental Europe and the US. ai.en: Common Ground: Ireland in the EU, an EPIC exhibition on Ireland's joining of the European Economic Community in 1973.

events.description: Ireland joined the European Economic Community (EEC) – as the EU was then known – on January 1, 1973, after a referendum endorsed by 83% of voters. It was then among the poorest and most underdeveloped countries in western Europe, with a population just over half of its current size. Ireland’s accession proved to be the most consequential economic milestone in the half century since Irish independence, but it also set in motion far-reaching social and cultural change. EU legislation has driven improvements in workers’ rights, for example, and set binding targets for climate action. Irish people have studied and built new lives across Europe, while many Europeans have since made their homes here in Ireland.

title.en: Legends, Ghosts and Ghouls of Dublin | Walking Tour

ai.en: A walking tour of Dublin's legends, ghosts and ghouls, from Merrion Square.

events.description: Ireland has a unique relationship with its legendary past. Kept alive in the histories of the Filí and the Seanchaidhe, Ireland’s gods were not destroyed but - in the words of Mark Williams - demoted to lesser beings. This is an important element of Ireland’s oral histories, which in turn have coloured its popular histories and left many legends for us to parse over today. On the other side of Irish history we have the ballrooms, the salons, and the private studies of Dublin’s litterati. The seances and unwrapping parties, the mysteries and the macabre, all combining into the secret esoteric orders that strove to unlock the secrets of existence. ai.en: Grisly tales from the Anglo-Norman advance, a talk at the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies on the horrors of the twelfth century.

events.description: Their conquests and institutions reshaped the island’s political and cultural landscape, creating an Ireland of ‘two nations’. This talk explores the violent reality of their impact and how Irish kings sought to respond. It also considers the limits of conquest and the ethnic tensions that emerged as expansion stalled. Political and military deadlock left both communities in limbo, with each increasingly viewing the other as an existential threat. Their worsening relations and deeply felt grievances offer a compelling study of conflict and coexistence, with wider relevance to our understanding of colonial societies. title.en: Legends, Ghosts and Ghouls of Dublin | Walking Tour

ai.en: A walking tour of Dublin's legends, ghosts and ghouls, from Merrion Square.

events.description: Ireland has a unique relationship with its legendary past. Kept alive in the histories of the Filí and the Seanchaidhe, Ireland’s gods were not destroyed but - in the words of Mark Williams - demoted to lesser beings. This is an important element of Ireland’s oral histories, which in turn have coloured its popular histories and left many legends for us to parse over today. On the other side of Irish history we have the ballrooms, the salons, and the private studies of Dublin’s litterati. Come explore with us where these two elements fuse to create the wonderful world of Legends, Ghosts, and Ghouls that are part of Dublin’s history. ai.en: Halloween and its creepy Irish origins, a talk at the Tree of Gold on the supernatural roots of the festival.

events.description: Want a chilling experience? Not too chilling — we want you entertained, not terrified. But we do venture into the supernatural and the origins behind Halloween customs we still enjoy today. Halloween began as a Christian overlay on the ancient Irish feast of Samhain. The Celts revered their ancestors — and feared them too. On this night, the veil between worlds thinned and spirits, mostly malevolent, walked the land. People devised tactics to protect themselves, customs that survive today as Halloween traditions. Irish writers drew on this folklore for their own spectral creations — The Picture of Dorian Gray, Melmoth the Wanderer, Carmilla, and Dracula. We'll dip into it all, and try not to get splashed in blood!

ai.en: The CHQ Tour at EPIC, exploring the heritage of the Docklands area and the building's stories.

events.description: This is a rare opportunity to explore the rich heritage of the Docklands area and uncover the unique story behind the building, its architecture, and its role in shaping the city. The CHQ Building, originally known as Stack A, was constructed in the early 19th century as part of the broader Custom House docks complex. This tour offers the chance to step back in time and discover the building’s original purpose as a bonded warehouse for storing valuable cargo including tobacco, tea, wine and spirits. On the CHQ tour, you’ll also hear the fascinating story of its transformation into a grand Banqueting Hall in 1856, when thousands gathered for an enormous celebration in honour of Irish soldiers returning from the Crimean War.

ai.en: An Ireland's Christmas Traditions walking tour from the Tree of Gold in Central Plaza.

events.description: Did the Irish invent Christmas? Not quite—but it's not entirely a myth either! Soak up the festive atmosphere amid twinkling lights, beautifully decorated shop windows, public cribs, and a few modest street markets on this engaging walking tour. Discover St Nicholas's surprising Irish connections too. events.description: Ardal O'Hanlon Live at Fitzpatrick Castle Hotel, Killiney on Jan, 31st 2027 - Part of Dalkey Comedy Festival. Ardal O Hanlon - Not Himself: Oh, it’s all there! All the trademarks are in evidence in Ardal’s latest show. Beautifully crafted stand-up comedy? Yes. Celebrated use of language? Tick. Lateral thinking, surreal flourishes, sharp observations? Of course. As for the occasional profundity? Maybe. Despite his best attempts over many decades to put the world to rights, it is still a colossal mess. And so, Ardal has no choice but to go out on the road again. Like the good comedy doctor he is, he fearlessly diagnoses the various pathologies and neuroses that are currently ravaging humanity. Disclaimer: No solutions provided. After an alarming experience at the supermarket, Ardal reflects on who he is as a man and a comedian. He examines his own ethnic and religious background. And thinks twice about the very core of his identity as a voice of reason. Is everything a big lie? With no major trauma of his own to draw on for material, apart from the drag of getting older, he also turns his gaze outwards at the joys and follies of contemporary life. Towel Animals? A.I.? Chair Yoga? Cauliflower as a main course? Yes. Yes. Yes. And Yes. No current idiocy is left unexamined. With a highly developed sense of the ridiculous, and proper comedy bones, NOT HIMSELF, is a testament to the healing power of humour. And the joy of jokes. ai.en: Frederick Douglass and his Irish connections at the Ambassador Theatre, about the abolitionist and orator.

events.description: Frederick Douglass (1818–1895) was a renowned African American abolitionist, orator, publisher and author—reportedly the most photographed American of the 19th century. Recently escaped from slavery, Douglass arrived in Dublin in 1845, staying four months to publish his first autobiography, deliver lectures, and meet activists like Daniel O'Connell. He later made four visits to Belfast in 1846. We'll explore Dublin sites tied to his time here, set against political change: relief for Irish Catholics, yet widespread poverty and a famine gripping the countryside. Douglass was deeply moved by Ireland's underclass and those working to relieve it. Readers are advised to check with the organiser before relying on the details published here.

events.description: WILLA WHITE: DEAD MAN TALKING Following a year which saw him sell out both the 3Olympia Theatre and The Gaiety Theatre (the first comedian to do so in over 10 years), Dublin comedian Willa White will debut his brand new stand-up show Dead Man Talking at the Abbey Tavern, Howth on 4th April 2026. Willa White has exploded in popularity over the past 18 months, quickly marking himself out as one of the biggest names in the Irish comedy circuit. Having sold over 10,000 tickets to date. As well as comedy, Willa has taken to acting, performing in the multi-award-winning production The Examination with Irish theatre company Brokentalkers, and just completed a three-night run in The Ambassador Theatre (a venue at which Willa became the first ever comedian to hold a residency). He has also taken to podcasting, seeing his show You Must Be Jokin’, which he co-hosts with fellow Dublin comedian Eric Lalor, fly to the top of the Irish podcast charts. With support slots alongside Jason Byrne, Tommy Tiernan, Kevin Bridges and John Bishop ticked off the list, Willa is ready to kick start the newest phase of his comedy journey. His newest show Dead Man Talking will see Willa explore his belief that he realistically should have been dead long before the family and friends who’ve gone before him, after attempting to take his own life in 1991. Dead Man Talking will see Willa reflect on memories of those who have passed, and the fun times they shared on this rollercoaster we call life. This is a…

events.description: The Dublin Riviera is a guided coastal walk back to a golden era where local residents and visitors wined and dined in the yacht clubs, restaurants and hotels along the waterfront, and danced in the Pavilion, the ballrooms and the nightclubs. The walk will provide an insight into the symbiotic relationship between the harbour and the town and how this helped Dún Laoghaire to evolve into an elegant and glamorous centre of hospitality, entertainment and luxurious bathing, a “Dublin Riviera”. events.description: Ireland's premier whiskey tasting event, Whiskey Live Dublin is back once again! Showcasing both the long established and new arrivals to the Irish whiskey scene, sample the latest Irish whiskey releases as well as whiskies from across the globe including Scotland, Japan and the U.S.A. Delicious whiskey and food pairings, informative masterclasses (some of the 2026 favourites included a Pappy Van Winkle masterclass, Redbreast, Dunville's, Dingle masterclasses and a cocktail tasting experience with The Sexton Irish Whiskey) and whiskey cocktails from some of Dublin's most esteemed bartenders will all be present at this year's Whiskey Live. As per previous years, the event will also feature the ever expanding range of other Irish craft spirits and some craft beers and food pairings. events.description: David McSavage brings his new show, 'SAYS I To YOU' to The Purty Kitchen, Dún Laoghaire - on Sat, April 17th SAYS I TO YOU Sometimes McSavage is actually shocked by the things he says on stage, a potentially dangerous problem, but fortunately he can’t really be cancelled because he’e not that successful, and can always go back street performing. McSavages new show was going to be called “Pig Ignorant” inspired by the collapsed personalities that live among us, making life shite and occasionally unbearable. Then his Father died, themes from old show linger though like annoying tenants living rent free in his head, but the end game, the final curtain, and all the ignominious tragic/comic drama surrounding the death of his Father have taken over.
